title: How long is the middle finger of {{NAME_2}}?
description: The palm is taken away from the whole hand by breaking one unit into ten tenths, and the answer is checked by changing both lengths to tenths. Keeko doubts the tenths and takes the smaller number from the bigger one.
teaching_notes: One idea: when there are too few tenths to take away, break one unit into ten tenths. Watch for students who take the smaller tenths from the bigger tenths whichever length they belong to.

source: The hand is 12 4/10 units long and the palm is 6 7/10 units. How long is the middle finger? Solve it by breaking a unit, and check by converting to tenths.
video_script.why: The child has added lengths with units and tenths and now takes one length away from another when the tenths are too few.
video_script.substitution: When the tenths are too few, break one unit into ten tenths, then take away units and tenths separately.
video_script.anchor: A hand with its palm marked from the wrist and the middle finger as the rest, drawn along a unit scale
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the smaller tenths number from the bigger one, 7 - 4 = 3, and 12 - 6 = 6, to get 6 3/10, but the 4 tenths of the hand cannot give up 7 tenths, so a unit must be broken.
video_script.payoff_line: The middle finger is five and seven tenths units long

names.{{NAME_2}}: the child whose hand, palm and middle finger are measured

maths_rules: Break 1 unit of the 12 into 10 tenths: 12 4/10 = 11 + 10/10 + 4/10 = 11 14/10.
14/10 - 7/10 = 7/10 and 11 - 6 = 5, so the answer is 5 units and 7/10, which is 5 7/10.
Slip: 7 - 4 = 3 and 12 - 6 = 6 gives 6 3/10, but 4 tenths cannot give up 7 tenths.
video_script.design: One idea: when there are too few tenths, break one unit into ten tenths. Assumes the child can add units and tenths and change them to tenths. Wrong idea: take the smaller tenths number from the bigger one. The hand stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a hand of 12 4/10 units with its palm of 6 7/10 units marked from the wrist, and the rest of the middle finger marked in a different colour

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.hand: the hand appears on the scale, 12 4/10 units long
marks.palm: the palm is marked from the wrist, 6 7/10 units long
marks.ask: the part of the middle finger beyond the palm glows

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>The hand of {{NAME_2}} is twelve and four tenths units long.
<bookmark mark='palm'/>The palm is six and seven tenths units long.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The middle finger is the rest of the hand. How long is it?

beats.on_screen: the hand and the palm stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 4 tenth-parts and 7 tenth-parts side by side with a cross on taking 7 from 4; then one unit bar breaks into 10 parts labelled 1/10

marks.few: 4 small parts sit beside 7 small parts and taking 7 from 4 is crossed out
marks.break: one whole unit bar breaks into 10 parts labelled 1/10

narration: <bookmark mark='few'/>Four tenths are fewer than seven tenths, so we cannot take seven tenths from four tenths.
<bookmark mark='break'/>But one whole unit can be broken into ten tenths. That gives us more tenths to take from.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the hand is twelve and four tenths units. The palm is six and seven tenths units.

beats.on_screen: To find: the length of the middle finger; check in tenths

marks.find: the words middle finger and check in tenths are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the length of the middle finger, and then check the answer in tenths.

marks.tenths: the 4/10 and the 7/10 are circled with the sign for less than

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, take the palm away from the hand.
<bookmark mark='tenths'/>Look at the tenths. We have only four tenths, but we must take away seven tenths.

marks.two: one unit of the 12 breaks into 10/10 and joins the 4/10

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, break one unit of the twelve into ten tenths.
<bookmark mark='new'/>Twelve units and four tenths becomes eleven units and fourteen tenths.

marks.units: 11 - 6 = 5 is written and joined with the 7/10

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, subtract the tenths and then the units. Fourteen tenths take away seven tenths leaves seven tenths.
<bookmark mark='units'/>Eleven units take away six units leaves five units.

marks.four: both lengths change to tenths: 124/10 and 67/10
marks.diff: 124/10 - 67/10 = 57/10 is written and matched with the answer

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, check in tenths. The hand is one hundred twenty four tenths, and the palm is sixty seven tenths.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>The difference is fifty seven tenths, which is five units and seven tenths. It matches.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The middle finger is five and seven tenths units long.
Both ways give the same answer.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows tenths: 7 - 4 = 3, units: 12 - 6 = 6; the 4 tenths of the hand cannot give up 7 tenths; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 4 small parts try to give up 7 and cannot
marks.cant: the 7 small parts are crossed out of the 4 and a unit bar glows

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the finger is six and three tenths units, because seven minus four is three.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the hand has four tenths, and the palm is taken from the hand. <bookmark mark='cant'/>We cannot take seven tenths from four tenths, so a unit must be broken first.
